answer: Use the capabilities command: 'show capabilities-<name>', where 'name' is the name of the card (string, no default). It retrieves the information about that card's capabilities. The command is available in Operational mode and in Candidate Configuration mode. It is a show-only object: there is no add, set or delete form. For capability data indexed by card type rather than by an installed card instance, the related objects are supported-card (per card-type), supported-port (per card-type/port-name), supported-slot and supported-tom.

To provision a card you use 'add card-<name>' and must supply three mandatory attributes: required-type (the card type, String length 0..32, for example CHM1R, CHM6, CHM7, XMM4, UTM2, FAN, PEM, BLANK), chassis-name (String length 1...255, default 1) and slot-name (String). Optional attributes on add are required-subtype, card-mode, subslot-name, power-profile, alias-name, admin-state (lock/maintenance/unlock, default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default Inhibited) and label. subslot-name can only be set at (sub)card creation. Example: add card-1-4 required-type CHM1R chassis-name 1 slot-name 2.

On 1830 GX G40 you must set the chassis ambient temperature to 40C before a Native ZR TOM will come up. If configured-ambient-temperature is not set, the system raises a port config mismatch alarm and the TOM cannot be provisioned. The attribute is configured-ambient-temperature on the chassis object, a number in Celsius units, settable with 'add chassis-<name>' or 'set chassis-<name> configured-ambient-temperature <value>' and readable with 'show chassis-<name> configured-ambient-temperature'. It has no default. It is the value used to compute the FRU's power consumption.

The console object carries baud-rate, set with 'set console-<name> baud-rate <value>' and read with 'show console-<name> [baud-rate] [actual-baud-rate] [auto-sensing-state] [local-switch] [status]'. Permitted values are auto-sensing, 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600 and 115200. The default is 9600 on 1830 GX G30 and 115200 on 1830 GX G40. Yes, it can work it out itself: with auto-sensing the system detects the baud rate from 'ENTER' presses on the serial console client, then locks it; the detected rate appears in actual-baud-rate and auto-sensing-state shows sensing or locked (default sensing). Not all cards support auto-sensing; check console-port-support and default-console-baud-rate on supported-card.

Use 'show controller-card-<name> [redundancy-status] [redundancy-standby-status] [number-of-switchover-events] [time-of-last-switchover] [additional-details]'. redundancy-status is active, standby or not-in-service (default not-in-service). redundancy-standby-status tells you readiness: ready-synchronized means the standby controller is in sync and ready; other values are not-ready-synchronizing (default), not-ready-synchronize-fail, lock-out (protection in lock-out) and card-not-present. number-of-switchover-events (uint32) and time-of-last-switchover are only visible on the active controller card. additional-details is a string (0..128) with extra synchronization detail.

Use 'show equipment [<option>]', available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. With no option it displays all installed equipment; the available options vary according to your installation. To restrict output to one card, give the card object as the option, for example 'show equipment card-1-1'. The per-card output lists the child objects (controller-card-1-1, console-1-1, port-1-1-AUX-1, port-1-1-CRAFT, port-1-1-DCN, port-1-1-U1) and the card attributes: required-type, required-subtype, category, chassis-name, slot-name, max-power-draw, last-reboot-reason, alias-name, AID, admin-state, oper-state, avail-state, alarm-report-control and label.

Both are controlled by equipment-policies: 'set equipment-policies [tom-auto-migration <value>] [auto-assigned-directions <value>] [auto-assigned-degrees <value>] [cable-id-control <value>] [chassis-assignment-mode <value>] [comm-eth-location <value>]'. tom-auto-migration (enabled/disabled) enables automatic update of the TOM subtype based on the present equipment; it may directly impact existing configurations and it covers subtype migration only, not TOM type migration (no update between QSFPDD and QSFP28). auto-assigned-degrees (enabled/disabled) is disabled by default, but enabled if l0-mode-op is hsc-ols, so degrees are not assigned automatically unless you enable it. auto-assigned-directions is enabled by default.

You have to enable it. 'set equipment-templates use-serdes-templates <value>' turns SerDes templates on globally; values are enabled and disabled, default disabled (the CLI value completion offers false and true). On enabling, templates are not applied retroactively: they are applied from that moment onward. On disabling there is no impact, and the existing SerDes configuration is kept on all TOMs whether it came from a template or was set manually. Read it back with 'show equipment-templates use-serdes-templates'. Application of any serdes-template depends on this flag being true; use apply-template to force re-application.

Use 'show fru-info-<manifest-file>/<equipment-type>'. It displays the packaged FRU information associated with a particular equipment-type. manifest-file is the manifest file, a string of length 0..256; equipment-type is the type of the equipment, a string of length 0..32. Neither has a default. The command is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode and is show-only. For the data of a physically present FRU (serial number, CLEI, part number, hardware version) use the inventory command instead.

Use the inventory command, which shows data for a present FRU: 'show inventory-<name>', 'show inventory-<chassis-name>-<slot-name>', 'show inventory-<card-name>-<port-name>' or 'show inventory-<card-name>.<slot-name>'. Request serial-number (Serial number of the equipment) and clei (Common Language Equipment Identifier), both strings. Other attributes available on the same object are hardware-version, actual-type, actual-subtype, sw-support-revision (default 0), PON, vendor, part-number, manufacture-date and insertion-date (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ or 'NA'), number-of-lanes, vendor-compliance-code, actual-power-class, actual-max-power-draw and fw-status. Example: show inventory-1-3-1.

Use 'show led-<location>/<name> [status]' or 'show leds'. location is the AID of the equipment location of the LED (chassis, card or port AID, string 1..32) and name is the LED name within the FRU (string 1..16). The object exists even if the FRU is not physically present; in that case status reads not-available, which is also the default. The status values are: not-available, off, yellow, flashing-yellow, green, flashing-green, red, flashing-red, cycling-with-off (cycles all supported colors including off), cycling (cycles all colors excluding off, used for lamp test), amber and flashing-amber. Example LEDs: led-1-1/active, led-1-1/fault, led-1-PEM-1/status.

In 1830 GX G40 there are three physical categories: comm-eth, USB and trib/line. comm-eth and USB ports exist on XMMs only and are found on Slot 1 XMMs. The trib/line ports appear on a CHM6 or CHM7 (slots 4-7) only after a TOM is provisioned in that CHM6/CHM7. Port objects are managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. The port-type attribute, shown with 'show port-<card-name>-<port-name> port-type', enumerates: line (colored CWDM/DWDM line-side module), tributary (grey client interfaces), tributary-subport (a tributary split into subports), usb, comm, uplink (aggregation ports to an adjunct line function), optical, otdr, ocm and pluggable (the L0 module cage for a QSFP/SFP/SFP+ TOM).

Use 'show resources-<name> [internal-cell-switch-total-bandwidth] [internal-cell-switch-available-bandwidth] [paired-slot-total-bandwidth] [paired-slot-available-bandwidth]'. These four bandwidth attributes apply only to SPN2/SPN2C cards; the paired-slot pair applies only to SPN2/SPN2C cards that support Paired Slots. Internal cell-switch total and available bandwidth default to 600.000 Gbit/s when the card has paired slot interconnection capability. Paired-slot total and available bandwidth default to 500.000 Gbit/s with that capability and to 0 without it. The same object also shows supported-carriers, unassigned-carriers and supported-sub-components. Example: show resources-254-1.

Read the status leaf on the serdes object: 'show serdes-<card-name>-<port-name>/<serdes-name> [value] [status]'. status is the state of the advanced parameter as observable on the system once it is configured, with values set (parameter set), unknown (parameter unknown, the default), in-progress (parameter in progress), failed (parameter failed) and not-supported (parameter not supported). A bare 'show serdes' lists every parameter with its value and status, for example serdes-1-7-T1/TxEQ 1 set. The parameter itself is created with 'add serdes-<card-name>-<port-name>/<serdes-name> value <value>', changed with set, and removed with delete.

A serdes-template is keyed by TOM part number and is created per tom-part-number: 'add serdes-template-<name> [tom-part-number <value>] [card-types-applicable <value>] [ports-applicable <value>]'. tom-part-number is a string of length 1..16. Templates apply to all line cards that support serdes; when a TOM with that part-number is plugged in the template is applied automatically. You can narrow the ports with ports-applicable, whose values are 'all' (the default behavior: all ports considered) or port names, string length 1..16, maximum 20 elements. Manual serdes configuration is still allowed and kept even when it deviates from the template. Swapping in a TOM with a different part-number resets the serdes configuration and re-applies the new template if one exists. Application depends on use-serdes-templates being true; force re-application with apply-template.

Each individual parameter is a serdes-template-entry, composed of a serdes parameter name and its value: 'add serdes-template-entry-<serdes-template-name>/<serdes-template-entry-name> value <value>'. Edit with 'set serdes-template-entry-<serdes-template-name>/<serdes-template-entry-name> [value <value>]', remove with delete, and display with 'show serdes-template-entry-<serdes-template-name>/<serdes-template-entry-name>/<name> [value]'. name is the name of the serdes parameter, string length 0..256; value is the value of the serdes parameter, string length 0..256; tom-part-number identifies the template, string length 1..16. Example: add serdes-template-entry-T-DQ4CNT-NIN/RxEQ value 3.

Yes. The serial-console object holds the global configuration of all serial console ports in the system and is managed by the system, so it cannot be manually deleted. Use 'set serial-console [global-switch <value>] [global-timeout <value>]' and 'show serial-console [global-switch] [global-timeout]'. global-switch allows access by serial console, values enabled and disabled, default enabled; each console port can override this global behavior via the console object's local-switch (use-global-switch, force-enable, force-disable). global-timeout is the serial console inactivity timeout, a number in minutes, default 60, and can be set to zero to disable the inactivity timer. Example: set serial-console global-switch enabled global-timeout 80.

Use the slot equipment holder object: 'show slot-<chassis-name>-<slot-name> [AID] [supported-type] [installed-type] [oper-state] [avail-state] [current-equipment]', or 'show slot-<card-name>.<slot-name>' for a subslot. current-equipment names the equipment currently required in this slot (for example 1-1). installed-type is what is physically there and supported-type lists what the slot accepts, for example CHM6,gx:UCM4 on slots 5-7 of a G42. oper-state is enabled or disabled (default disabled) and avail-state reports values such as normal in-service or partially-faulted abnormal in-service. A bare 'show slot' lists every slot in the node. For what could go there by card type, see supported-slot possible-card-types.

Use 'show sub-component-<card-name>/<sub-component-name> [AID] [description]', available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. card-name is the card supporting the sub-component (string 0..64 characters), sub-component-name is the sub-component name, AID is the Resource Access Identifier (string 1..64) and description is a user configurable description (string 0..128). A bare 'show sub-component' lists them all, for example sub-component-1-6/dco-oec with AID 1-6-dco-oec, described as the DCO OEC (Optical Engine Controller) sub-component, and sub-component-1-6/dco-secproc, the DCO Security Processor. You can also see the names of a card's sub-components via 'show resources-<name> supported-sub-components', which lists those addressable for operations like restart.

Use 'show supported-card-<card-type> node-type-compatibility'. node-type-compatibility gives the supported NE node-type for a sled card and is only of relevance for line-cards and carrier-cards. The values are all (compatible with any node-type), ILA (In-Line Amplifier, two-directions) and OADM (Optical Add/Drop Multiplexer). So the card is usable on an in-line amplifier node if the value is ILA or all. The same command exposes sw-support-revision, supported-subtype, description, default-card-mode, supported-card-mode, card-width, card-height, is-field-replaceable, category, grid-mode-support, max-power-draw, leds, location-led-support, console-port-support, default-console-baud-rate, support-serdes-config, supported-bands and supported-features. Example: show supported-card-CHM1R.

Use 'show supported-chassis-<chassis-type>', where chassis-type is an identityref such as G31, G32, G34c or G42. controller-redundancy-supported is true or false and states whether that chassis supports controller redundancy. Slot counts come from number-of-front-slots and number-of-rear-slots, both uint8. For example supported-chassis-G42 reports controller-redundancy-supported true, power-control-supported true, depth 600 mm, height 3 RUs, 7 front slots and 12 rear slots. Other attributes are supported-subtype, default-subtype, description, fan-adjustment-on-altitude (default false), dust-filter-replacement (not-applicable, optional-dust-filter default, dust-filter-regularly-replaced), leds, supported-subchassis-type (max 10 elements; empty means no multi-chassis) and supported-features.

Use 'show supported-port-<card-type>/<port-name>', for example 'show supported-port-CHM1R/2'. port-type says what the port is for: line, tributary, tributary-subport, usb, comm, uplink, optical, otdr, ocm or pluggable (the L0 cage for a QSFP/SFP/SFP+ TOM). configuration-mode says who configures it: system-configured means the system configures it automatically and the user cannot make changes, user-configured means you can provision or de-provision. The object also exposes direction (not-applicable, tx, rx, rxtx), faceplate-label (1..36), leds (max 10), present (always, or in-node-controller-only), default-tom (default none), parent-port, subport-list, and allows-auto-migration (true/false, default true) which says whether TOMs on this port type follow the equipment-policies tom-auto-migration flag.

Use 'show supported-slot-<chassis-type>/<slot-name>' (or supported-slot-<card-type>/<slot-name> for subslots). requires-blank-when-empty answers the blank question with not-applicable, optional or required. On a G42, slots 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and PEM-1 through PEM-4 are 'required'; slot 2, the FAN slots and FANCTRL-1 are 'not-applicable'. possible-card-types lists which cards can go in the slot, maximum 15 elements, for example XMM4 for slot 1, IOPANEL for slot 2 and CHM6,UCM4 for slots 4-7. The same command shows slot-location (front/rear), slot-vertical-position, slot-horizontal-position, configuration-mode (system-configured or user-configured), auto-provision-capable, default-card, reset-power in W at 55 degrees C, virtual-slot (default false) and leds (max 10).

Use 'show supported-tom-<card-type>/<port-name>/<tom-type>/<tom-subtype-group> [supported-subtype] [supported-phy-modes] [default-phy-mode]'. tom-type is the form factor, for example CFP2-DCO, QSFP28 or QSFPDD; tom-subtype-group is a string of length 0..32, for example '4x100GE-breakout'. supported-phy-mode gives the phy-modes supported by that TOM on that card and default-phy-mode gives the one used by default; both take values from 100GE, 200GE, 400GE, 2x100GE, 4x100GE, 100G, 4x10G, 4x10GE, 1GE, 2G5, 10G, 10GE, 2G5E, 40GE, 40G, 4x100G and 200G. supported-subtype lists the subtypes allowed for that TOM type in that card/port. Examples: show supported-tom-CHM1R/6/QSFP28 and show supported-tom-CHM1R/6/QSFPDD/2x100GE-breakout.

Use 'show supported-tom-power-<card-type>/<port-name>/<tom-type> [supported-power-class] [supported-max-power-draw]', where tom-type is the pluggable form factor identity matching the TOM required-type (for example CFP2-DCO, QSFP28, QSFPDD). supported-power-class is the maximum MSA power class the host port supports for that pluggable type, uint8 in the range 1..8; the port may only partially support that class, so read supported-max-power-draw, a decimal64 giving the maximum power in watts the host port allows for that pluggable type under supported-power-class. What the fitted module actually reports is on the inventory object as actual-power-class (uint8, 1..8) and actual-max-power-draw, populated only for third-party transceiver subtypes on hosts that enforce power-class rules.
